external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member who uses the app or a kiosk to borrow, renew, reserve, or return books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
external_entities.notes: Members also scan their library card and books at kiosks.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who use the circulation page to change loan and member account records.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: Everyone at the desk uses the same shared login for the circulation page.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: A phone application through which members request loan renewals and reservations and which calls the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.
processes.notes: The app says which book and which member, and asks for titles for reservations.

processes.name: kiosk
processes.description: A self-service branch kiosk that accepts member cards and scanned books and sends loans and returns to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
processes.notes: The text does not establish whether kiosks communicate directly with the loans database.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST API that is the service's interface for app, kiosk, and desk circulation operations and that reads and writes the loans database.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: Lending service note says the API is internal-only; Interview transcript says phones talk straight to it over the internet. The API is one service with no queue in front of it. Authentication behavior is uncertain: Priya said, "I think it checks a token" and could not say what it accepts or does with rejected calls.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The database containing members, loans, reservations, names, email addresses, home addresses, and full borrowing histories.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: The two databases were merged in the spring; the old reservations database is gone.

data_flows.name: request loan change
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to renew a loan or reserve a title.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
data_flows.notes: The app has behavior of its own and then calls the lending API.

data_flows.name: write loan change
data_flows.description: The app calls the lending API with a member and book or title to renew a loan or place a reservation.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.notes: The API's phone-call authentication is unknown; Priya said, "I think it checks a token" and could not confirm what it accepts.
data_flows.data_description: Member, book, loan renewal, or reservation request

data_flows.name: scan book transaction
data_flows.description: A member scans their library card and books at a branch kiosk for borrowing or returning.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.notes: The member's scan interaction with the kiosk is described, but its protocol and authentication are not stated.
data_flows.data_description: Library card and book scan for a loan or return

data_flows.name: send loan return
data_flows.description: A kiosk sends each scanned loan and return to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API.
data_flows.notes: The kiosk-to-database path is unknown; the interview says only that the speaker sees what arrives at the API.
data_flows.data_description: Loan or return record with member and book information

data_flows.name: change loan account
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page served by the lending API to extend loans, clear account blocks, or mark books returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.
data_flows.notes: Everyone at the desk uses one shared login; the password is on a card taped under the desk. The history records that a loan was closed by hand but not which person or branch performed it.
data_flows.data_description: Manual loan and member account changes

data_flows.name: read-write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.notes: The database contains member, loan, reservation, contact, address, and borrowing-history data.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations, and borrowing histories

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which branch kiosks and desk staff operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.
trust_boundaries.notes: Desk staff are also stated to work on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data centre where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

trust_boundaries.name: member phone
trust_boundaries.description: The member's phone on which the library app runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.
trust_boundaries.notes: The phone is treated as a customer-controlled device boundary.

assumptions.assumption: The library app runs in a customer-controlled device zone represented by the member phone boundary.
assumptions.basis: The interview states that the app is on the member's phone; a member phone is treated as the customer's own device.
The interview states that phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet.
The database contains names, email addresses, home addresses, and full member borrowing histories, whose disclosure harms persons.
